title: EFB live book snapshot
description: One object per run, written by scripts/run_live_daily.py to Cloudflare R2 as latest.json and snapshots/<close>.json, and read by the Cloudflare page through an R2 binding. The writer is tested against this schema, so the writer and the page cannot drift. JSON has no NaN: every number is a number or null, and null means the run did not have it.

generated_at.description: UTC, when the snapshot was built.

target_close.description: The session the book is priced from.

book_as_of.description: The close of the proposal the book came from. On a stopped run this is the previous proposal's close, never the target, so the page cannot show a book without its date.

expected_next_by.description: The UTC instant by which the next run's snapshot should already exist: the next NYSE session at the cron's own slot plus the stated grace. Past it, the page is in a failure state.

store.description: Where the run's writes went, or why they could not go anywhere.

status.description: Every value except ok and market_closed is a failure state on the page. market_closed is a day the exchange was shut: no close to price, so no run was due.

notify_status.description: What the evening's message did. Written as `pending` because the snapshot is published before the message is sent, and rewritten by the 15:30 UTC fills reconciliation from the evening's own `run_status` row, which holds the truth: `pending` and `sent` are both ordinary and the page says nothing about either, while `failed` means the owner was never told and is the one state the page warns about.

establishment.description: True when the run created the book from an empty account: it may trade up to the full book and the daily traded-notional brake starts on the second trading day.

cost_label.description: What the day's cost number is the cost of: building the book from flat (establishment) or a rebalance. The proposal's cost is the establishment cost, so a rebalance day must not read as though it were one.

construction.description: Generated from the proposal's own fields, never asserted beside it.

positions.description: The paper account's book against the store's, read before the orders were built. matches is null when the account could not be read, which is a different answer from an account that holds nothing.

breadth.description: There is no unqualified n_eff anywhere in this document: n_eff_kept is the book that trades and n_eff_full_book is the 499-name book before the floor, each with its label.

reason.description: Why the book is empty, when it is: a stopped run whose store holds no proposal shows no names and this sentence. Null when the book has names.

gross.description: The gross of the book that trades: the kept set after the hedge, renormalized to exactly 1.0 (100%).

gross_notional.description: That book's gross in dollars, so the headline gross is 100% and $1,000,000 rather than a fraction alone.

full_book_gross.description: The 499-name book's gross after sizing and before the floor - no variance cap, because the cap is applied to the kept set. A different book, shown only as a labelled detail, never as the gross.

net.description: The traded book's net, the kept set after the hedge.

full_book_net.description: The 499-name book's net, beside the traded book's rather than as "the net".

achieved_annual_vol.description: The traded book's forecast annual volatility: the book the owner holds.

full_book_achieved_annual_vol.description: The 499-name book's forecast annual volatility, shown beside the traded book's rather than as the book's forecast.

traded_notional.description: The dollars the evening traded in this name, as the absolute notional of the leg it built for it - 0 for a name it built no leg for, including the kept names the $250 minimum left untraded. `weight` is the holding and this is the movement, so the two answer different questions about the same name: the trades-by-reason table sums both, and the turnover it reports is this column, not a difference between two books. Null when the book was published by a run that carried no orders.

expected_cost_split.description: The same expected cost, split the way the proposal computes it, in basis points of NAV. `trading` is spread + impact + commission, which is the only half a fill price can be measured against; `borrow` is the short leg's financing over the horizon, which no fill price pays, and comparing execution against it would be comparing a fill to a calendar. Absent on a manifest written before the breakdown existed, and never invented from the total.

borrow.description: The holding cost of the short leg over the horizon, not a year.

total.description: trading + borrow, which is `expected_cost_bps` on this same block by construction.

exposures_before_hedge.description: X'w of the pre-hedge book, one value per design column, named by fx.ESTIMATED_NAMES. This is the hedge's own X'w, taken from the sizing step rather than reconstructed, and it is clearly nonzero.

exposures_after_hedge.description: X'w after the FMP hedge, on the same labels. The hedge neutralizes every factor, so these are zero to within floating point.

traded_risk.description: The traded book's risk figures under their own names: forecast_annual_vol, idio_share, max_abs_exposure, gross, net, n_eff, max_weight, variance_share_cap_binds, top_variance_shares. Read from the proposal manifest, so the page, the reconciliation row and the run_status row cannot disagree.

full_risk.description: The full book's risk figures under their own names: forecast_annual_vol, idio_share, max_abs_exposure, gross, net, n_eff, n_names.

unexplained_adjustment.description: The part of the day's realised P&L that no order of the loop's explains: a position that left the account with nothing behind it, as its own labelled figure rather than a correction applied to the P&L. Negative for a removal, zero on a day nothing left. The evening writes it, because the evening owns the day's P&L, from the same read as the `exits` block above. The key is absent, not null, on a document built without a reconciled row: there is no P&L to adjust, and an invented zero would read as a measured one.

actual_holdings.description: The account's own book beside the target book above, written by the evening run from the account read it makes before it sizes and rewritten by the 15:30 UTC fills reconciliation with what those orders did. Both writers fill the same block, and `read_by` says which one it was: the evening's read is the book the orders were measured against and has no close and no fills, because nothing has settled into it yet. The key is absent, not null, when nobody has read the account (a run that could not reach the broker, and the store's fallback book is not the account): a null key would read as an account holding nothing, which is a different statement from an account nobody read.

as_of.description: When the account was read, as a full timestamp (the page shows its date and time), by the run `read_by` names.

close.description: The evening whose orders settled into this book. Null on the evening's own read, which is taken before the orders go out.

read_by.description: Which run read the account: `evening` is the read the book was sized from, `morning` is the reconciliation that saw the fills. Carried rather than inferred from whether `fills` is present, because an evening read is not a morning on which nothing filled.

n_names.description: The number of names below, so the count and the list cannot disagree.

gross_notional.description: The sum of absolute notionals: what the account holds, both sides.

names.description: The held names, largest absolute notional first.

notional.description: Signed dollars, positive for a long.

weight.description: That notional over the account's equity, so it is comparable with the weights above.

fills.description: The evening's orders that produced this book, as the broker answered a read by id. Null when the book was written without a reconciliation.

trade_date.description: The close whose orders settled, which is the evening the notional belongs to.

n_orders.description: The legs the evening sent to the broker, which is the denominator a fill count is read against: a leg the evening decided against was never an order the broker could fill, and it is counted apart in `not_sent` rather than subtracted from this. The two sets are disjoint.

n_filled.description: Those the broker reports as filled.

n_unfilled.description: Those it reports as canceled, expired or rejected, or as only partly filled.

not_sent.description: Legs the evening decided against, so there is nothing at the broker to read. Counted apart from `n_orders`, which counts only the legs that were sent: the page shows `filled of n_orders` and states this beside it, because subtracting it from `n_orders` takes the never-sent legs out of a denominator they were never in.

realized_cost_bps.description: Signed slippage of the fill prices against the close, in basis points of NAV: positive is a cost. Null when no fill could be priced.

expected_cost_bps.description: The evening's own expectation for the same trade, from the reconciled row.

unfilled.description: One line per miss, as the email carries it: "DG sell_to_open 41 canceled 12:15 UTC".

unread.description: Orders the broker would not answer about, with the error. Distinct from a miss: the broker may have filled it.

not_sent_lines.description: One line per leg the evening could not send at all, with the reason derived here because the broker never saw the order and holds no record of it: "SKYD sell_to_open $500 never sent (SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND)". Only the legs no spelling could have traded - a ticker the broker's feed carries under no symbol - because the evening has already named its own decisions, the $250 minimum and the borrow among them.

realized_cost_avg_bps.description: The same realized cost averaged over every day the loop has reconciled, in basis points of NAV. One day is mostly the overnight move - the leg is sized after one close and fills at the next open - so this is the figure that can be read as execution quality. Null before any day has been priced.

realized_cost_days.description: How many days are behind the average. Stated with it because an average of two days is not an average of twenty, and because a day nothing could be priced on is not counted: an average over days nobody measured would be an average of the easy ones.

exits.description: The names the account held when it was last read and does not hold now, with nothing the loop did to explain them: no closing leg filled and no activity of the broker's names the ticker. Absent (not null) when the question was not asked, which is a different statement from an account where nothing left. This is the block behind the page's amber line about a position that walked out.

previous_read.description: The date of the broker read this block compares against, which is the evening that priced the previous close.

feed.description: Whether the broker's activity feed answered for the window. `not read` is not `nothing found`: the departure is still reported, with one fewer explanation checked, and the sentence says so rather than claiming the feed came back empty.

window.description: The window the activity feed was read for, from the day after the previous read to the read that noticed the name gone.

names.description: The departures, largest absolute notional first.

quantity.description: The shares the previous read held, signed as that read held them.

notional.description: The dollars that went with them, at the previous read's own market value.

risk.description: Per-name share of the book's predicted specific variance, for the page's concentration panel. Not written today: the sizing step caps that share at a fixed fraction, so the numbers exist inside the evening job's sizing call but the manifest does not carry them. The page hides the panel until this block is present rather than drawing it empty. `variance_share_cap` is the cap as a fraction, so 0.10 is the ten percent cap the sizing applies.

concentration.description: One entry per name, largest share first. Shares are fractions of the same total and add to one.

movers.description: What moved the book in the latest session, in dollars, for the page's movers panel. Not written today: the evening step that attributes a stored day lives on the E12 branch, and its per-name contributions are not in the manifest. The page hides the panel until this block is present.

session.description: The session the contributions belong to.

by_name.description: Per-name contribution to the session's P&L, in dollars, signed. The page shows the five best and the five worst.

by_sector.description: The same contributions summed by GICS sector, in dollars, signed. The sector names are the model's own, so they match the bundled map's labels.

bridge.description: The arithmetic between the three sets the page draws: the book the model sized, the orders the run sent and the positions the account holds. Each is correct on its own - 191 names, 199 orders and 188 positions on 2026-10-05 - and without this block they read as three disagreements rather than as one evening: which names were opened, which closed, which merely moved and which never traded at all. Every count is the writers' own, computed by `live/bridge.py` and published in this document so the page recomputes none of it and the two runs cannot disagree about a count. The evening writes the first half from the account read it makes and the legs it built, and the 15:30 UTC morning completes it with the fills and its own account read. The key is absent, not null, when no run built one (an evening that failed before its account read, or a morning with no published bridge to complete): a block of zeroes would read as an evening that moved nothing. Written by scripts/run_live_daily.py and scripts/reconcile_fills.py, and surfaced on the page as the book bridge panel.

close.description: The close the bridge is about: the session the evening sized for, which is the morning's own target_close when it completes the block.

seen_by.description: Which run wrote the block as it stands. `evening` means the fills and the account after are not in it yet and the three identities that need them are not checked; `morning` means it is complete.

book.description: The book's own size, so the count can be checked against the list the page draws rather than trusted.

held_before.description: The names the account held when the evening read it, before any of the evening's orders.

in_both.description: Names in both the held-before read and the new book: the names the evening considered trading.

opened.description: Names in the book and not held before: legs opened into a name the account did not have.

exited.description: Names held before and not in the book: positions closed out entirely.

changed.description: Names in both whose change was at least `under_minimum_usd`, which is the line between a leg worth an order and one the evening left alone.

under_minimum.description: Names in both whose change was under `under_minimum_usd`: legs the run built and did not send. They are the reason an order count can be smaller than a book, and on 2026-10-05 there were 34 of them.

orders_sent.description: Legs the run actually sent, from its own order rows rather than from a recount: a leg with a broker order id was sent, one without is a leg it decided against.

filled.description: Orders the 15:30 UTC reconciliation found filled. Null until the morning has completed the block.

did_not_fill.description: Orders sent and rejected. Null until the morning has completed the block.

held_after.description: Names the account held when the morning read it: the evening's held_before plus what it opened less what it closed, less any name that left with nothing behind it. Null until the morning has completed the block, never zero: a zero would read as an account holding nothing.

under_minimum_usd.description: The dollar line below which a continuing name is left untraded, $250.00 today, so the threshold the count was taken at travels with the count.

reversals_pending.description: Names the evening closed in order to reopen the other side at the next close, which explains part of the gap between the book and the account without an unexplained departure.

removed_without_order.description: Positions that left the account with no order of the loop's behind them, the PSKY case: the exit is a paper-keeping artifact and is carried on the reconciliation row as its own labelled adjustment, never netted out of the P&L in silence.

quantity.description: The shares the account held at the last read before it left.

notional.description: Those shares' dollars at that read, which is the figure on the reconciliation row.

unexplained.description: Names the book holds, the account does not, and neither list above accounts for. Empty on a bridge that adds up. A name here is the finding: the loop believes it holds something the account does not, which is what the PSKY disappearance was before Part B named it.

identities.description: Every identity the block claims, with both sides and whether each holds, checked by the runs that wrote the block. The page shows the ones that fail with their two figures rather than smoothing over them, so a bridge that does not add up is a finding and not a fourth number to trust.

holds.description: The block's verdict on its own identities: true when every one of them holds. False is a bridge that does not add up - a name the loop believes it holds and the account does not - and the page draws it in amber.

attribution.description: What the book earned, split into factor, idio, cost and the unexplained remainder, with the hedge's own factor P&L, the raw-beta line and the risk split beside it. Two periods of one shape: `live` is the book the loop actually traded, read from the store's attribution table by scripts/run_live_daily.py, which the evening run fills for every day it has not already attributed; `backtest` is the research panel's own seed artifact, a book nobody traded, and is null where the host's seed bundle does not carry it. The page opens on the live period.

live.description: The live book's own days, from the first day of the live period.

backtest.description: The research panel's 2012-2026 attribution, or null when the seed bundle on the host does not carry the artifact.

note.description: Why no live day is attributed yet, when none is. Empty means the section has something to show.

attribution_period.description: One attribution period: the days it holds, the sums over all of them, the most recent days themselves, and the risk split. The cumulative sums are over every day the period holds; `daily` is a bounded window of them, newest last, so a period that grows for years does not grow the payload.

label.description: What the period is, in words the page can print: the live book, or the research panel.

n_days.description: Days the period holds, which is the whole period, not the window below.

n_days_carried.description: How many of those days the `daily` window carries.

pnl_unexplained.description: The sum of the stored residuals: the panel's own return minus the three components above. Zero on a period whose artifacts reproduce the panel, and the fourth term the page draws so a day's four components reach its total.

max_identity_residual.description: The worst single day of total minus (factor + idio + cost). Not a sum: the identity is a per-day statement, and its worst day is what makes the split checkable.

n_computed_specific.description: Kept names whose residual was computed as r - X f because the model's own cross-section dropped them that session.

by_factor.description: Cumulative P&L per factor, keyed by the reported factor name.

pnl_unexplained.description: The day's own residual, and the term that makes the row add up: total minus (factor + idio + cost), to machine precision. It is the stored artifacts disagreeing with the panel's own return, not a fourth estimate, and the page draws it as its own band so a broken identity is visible.

pnl_timing.description: The hedge's own factor P&L for the day: the P&L the exposure gap between the two design vintages produced. On a book whose hedge did its job this is the part that should have been zero.

book_beta.description: Raw CAPM beta of the book, from the stored beta history, weighted by the day's holdings. Around 0.02 on the hedged live book, so the page prints it to three decimals.

pnl_beta.description: book_beta times market_return. It explains part of the idio P&L and is never added to the three components.

pre_hedge_vol.description: Annualized predicted volatility of the sized book the hedge acted on, from the same Sigma the hedged number uses. Null when the store's own alpha and specific volatility are not to hand.

hedged_vol.description: The same forecast at the book that was held. It is the number the hedge bought: pre_hedge_vol minus hedged_vol is what the hedge removed, which is what the panel draws rather than a flat line at 100% idiosyncratic.

factor_var_share.description: The book's predicted variance that the factors carry, as a fraction, from Sigma = X F X' + D at the book's own exposures. The hedged live book holds these near zero.

idio_var_share.description: The rest of the predicted variance: the specific diagonal, Sum w_i^2 D_ii.

monthly.description: The period's month sums, carried by the research panel so its chart is a decade without a decade of daily rows. Empty for the live period.

expected_trading_bps.description: The expected cost's trading half (spread + impact + commission), averaged over the days that carry one. This is the only half a realized fill cost can be measured against, because it is the half a fill price pays.

expected_borrow_bps.description: The short leg's holding cost over the horizon, averaged the same way. Shown beside the trading half rather than inside the number it is compared against: no fill price pays a calendar.

risk.description: The share of the book's predicted variance the factors carry, today and over the period, and the forecast volatility before and after the hedge, or null when no day of the period carries one.

note.description: What a reader has to know about this period: that it is a backtest, that a few rehearsal sessions were left out, that it is empty.
